records.source: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם יְרֻבַּ֜עַל ה֣וּא גִדְע֗וֹן וְכָל־הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ עַל־עֵ֣ין חֲרֹ֑ד וּמַחֲנֵ֤ה מִדְיָן֙ הָיָה־ל֣וֹ מִצָּפ֔וֹן מִגִּבְעַ֥ת הַמּוֹרֶ֖ה בָּעֵֽמֶק׃
records.gloss: And rose early Jerubbaal, he [is] Gideon, and all the people who [were] with him, and they camped by En-harod; and [the] camp of Midian was to him from [the] north, from [the] hill of the Moreh in the valley.
pieces: Early in the morning Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, and all the troops with him set up camp beside the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian lay to the north of them, by the hill of Moreh in the valley.

L.1: And Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) rose early, and all the people who [were] with him, and they camped beside En-harod; and the camp of Midian was on the north of him, from the hill of Moreh, in the valley.

R.1: Jerubbaal, who was also called Gideon, got up early with all his men, and they camped by the spring of Harod. The Midianite camp lay to their north, in the valley close to the hill of Moreh.

decisions.choice: Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon: one man with two names
decisions.reason: Gideon received the name Jerubbaal after he tore down Baal's altar; it was explained as "Let Baal contend against him" (6:32). The narrator uses both names so the reader knows they are the same man (also 8:29, 35).

decisions.choice: En-harod: "the spring of Harod", a name that sounds like "trembling"
decisions.reason: "En" means a spring. "Harod" sounds like the word for "trembling" that comes in verse 3, where everyone who is afraid and trembling is sent home. The place name fits what happens there.

decisions.choice: north of them, by the hill of Moreh in the valley: the Midianites were camped in the Valley of Jezreel
decisions.reason: The Midianites and their allies had crossed the Jordan and camped in the Valley of Jezreel (6:33). The hill of Moreh stands on the north side of that valley, across from Mount Gilboa, where the spring of Harod is usually placed. "To him" means relative to Gideon's camp.

decisions.choice: the people (Literal), the troops (Balanced), his men (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the ordinary word for "people", but here, as through this chapter, it means the fighting men Gideon had called out (6:34-35). Literal keeps "people"; Balanced says "troops" and Readable "men" so that the reader does not picture a crowd of families.

records.heading: Too many troops

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־גִּדְע֔וֹן רַ֗ב הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתָּ֔ךְ מִתִּתִּ֥י אֶת־מִדְיָ֖ן בְּיָדָ֑ם פֶּן־יִתְפָּאֵ֨ר עָלַ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יָדִ֖י הוֹשִׁ֥יעָה לִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Gideon, too many [is] the people who [are] with you for my giving Midian into their hand, lest glorify itself over me Israel, saying, my hand has saved me.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Gideon, "You have too many troops with you for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to hand Midian over to them. Israel would only boast against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and say, 'Our own strength has saved us.'

L.2: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Gideon, "The people who [are] with you [are] too many for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to give Midian into their hand, lest Israel glorify itself over {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, saying, 'My [own] hand has saved me.'

R.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Gideon, "You have too many men for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to give you victory over the Midianites. Israel would take the credit that belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and say, 'We saved ourselves by our own strength.'

decisions.choice: give Midian into their hand: give them victory over Midian
decisions.reason: "To give into the hand" of someone is to put an enemy in their power, to let them win (verses 7, 9, 14, 15; 3:28; 4:7).

decisions.choice: glorify itself over me: boast against God, claiming the honor that is his
decisions.reason: The verb means to take pride in oneself or to boast. With "over me" it describes taking for oneself the glory that belongs to God (compare Isaiah 10:15). "Lest" gives God's reason for cutting down the army.

decisions.choice: my hand has saved me: we won by our own strength
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. The LORD will make the army so small that no one can mistake the victory for Israel's own work (Deuteronomy 8:17; 1 Samuel 14:6; Psalm 44:4).

decisions.choice: Our own strength has saved us / We saved ourselves
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew, Israel speaks as one person ("my hand ... me"). Balanced and Readable use "we" and "us", as a people speaking of itself; Literal keeps the singular.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה קְרָ֨א נָ֜א בְּאָזְנֵ֤י הָעָם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מִֽי־יָרֵ֣א וְחָרֵ֔ד יָשֹׁ֥ב וְיִצְפֹּ֖ר מֵהַ֣ר הַגִּלְעָ֑ד וַיָּ֣שָׁב מִן־הָעָ֗ם עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּשְׁנַ֨יִם֙ אֶ֔לֶף וַעֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִ֖ים נִשְׁאָֽרוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And now, call please in [the] ears of the people, saying, whoever [is] afraid and trembling, let him turn back and depart from mount Gilead. And turned back of the people twenty and two thousand, and ten thousand remained.
pieces: Now announce to the troops, 'Whoever is afraid and trembling may turn back and leave Mount Gilead.'" So 22,000 of the troops turned back, and 10,000 were left.

L.3: And now, call out in the ears of the people, saying, 'Whoever [is] afraid and trembling, let him turn back and depart from Mount Gilead.'" And 22,000 of the people turned back, and 10,000 remained.

R.3: So announce to the men, 'Anyone who is afraid and shaking with fear may turn around and leave Mount Gilead.'" Then 22,000 men went home, and 10,000 stayed.

decisions.choice: whoever is afraid and trembling, let him turn back: the law for war applied to Gideon's army
decisions.reason: The law for going to war told the officers to send home anyone who was afraid, so that he would not make others lose heart (Deuteronomy 20:8). Here the LORD uses that rule to shrink the army. "Trembling" picks up the name of the spring of Harod (verse 1).

decisions.choice: depart: leave, perhaps quickly
decisions.reason: This verb is rare, and its sense here is not certain. It may mean to leave early or quickly, to turn around, or, if it is linked with the word for "bird", to fly off. Every option means that the fearful men go away.

decisions.choice: Mount Gilead: the reading of the Hebrew text, though its place is unclear
decisions.reason: Gilead is the land east of the Jordan, but Gideon is camped west of the river by the spring of Harod (verse 1). "Mount Gilead" may be a local name, otherwise unknown, for a height near the camp, or the text may once have read another name, such as Gilboa, the mountain beside Harod. No Hebrew manuscript is known to read differently; reviewers should check the manuscript notes.

decisions.choice: went home
decisions.reason: "Turned back" here means they left the army and went back to their homes; Readable says so plainly.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־גִּדְע֗וֹן עוֹד֮ הָעָ֣ם רָב֒ הוֹרֵ֤ד אוֹתָם֙ אֶל־הַמַּ֔יִם וְאֶצְרְפֶ֥נּוּ לְךָ֖ שָׁ֑ם וְהָיָ֡ה אֲשֶׁר֩ אֹמַ֨ר אֵלֶ֜יךָ זֶ֣ה׀יֵלֵ֣ךְ אִתָּ֗ךְ ה֚וּא יֵלֵ֣ךְ אִתָּ֔ךְ וְכֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁר־אֹמַ֜ר אֵלֶ֗יךָ זֶ֚ה לֹא־יֵלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֔ךְ ה֖וּא לֹ֥א יֵלֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Gideon, still the people [are] many; bring down them to the water, and I will refine them for you there; and it will be, [the one] of whom I say to you, this [one] will go with you, he will go with you; and every [one] of whom I say to you, this [one] will not go with you, he will not go.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Gideon, "There are still too many troops. Take them down to the water. I will sift them there for you. When I tell you, 'This one is to go with you,' he will go with you. But when I tell you, 'This one is not to go with you,' he will not go."

L.4: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Gideon, "The people [are] still [too] many. Bring them down to the water, and I will refine them for you there. And it shall be, the one of whom I say to you, 'This one shall go with you,' he shall go with you; and every one of whom I say to you, 'This one shall not go with you,' he shall not go."

R.4: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Gideon, "There are still too many men. Take them down to the water, and I will test them there and sort them out for you. If I say, 'This one will go with you,' he will go. If I say, 'This one will not go with you,' he will not go."

decisions.choice: refine them: test and separate them, as metal is refined
decisions.reason: The verb is used of melting metal to separate pure silver or gold from the waste (Psalm 12:7; Isaiah 1:25; Malachi 3:3). Here the LORD will sort the men and keep only those he chooses.

decisions.choice: this one will go ... he will go: the choice rests wholly with the LORD
decisions.reason: The sentence repeats itself on purpose: whoever the LORD names goes, and whoever he does not name does not. Gideon does not pick his own men.

decisions.choice: refine (Literal), sift (Balanced), test ... and sort them out (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of refining metal. Balanced uses "sift", which keeps the idea of separating; Readable says plainly what the LORD will do.

records.source: וַיּ֥וֹרֶד אֶת־הָעָ֖ם אֶל־הַמָּ֑יִםסוַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־גִּדְע֗וֹן כֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־יָלֹק֩ בִּלְשׁוֹנ֨וֹ מִן־הַמַּ֜יִם כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר יָלֹ֣ק הַכֶּ֗לֶב תַּצִּ֤יג אוֹתוֹ֙ לְבָ֔ד וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יִכְרַ֥ע עַל־בִּרְכָּ֖יו לִשְׁתּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And he brought down the people to the water; and said Yahweh to Gideon, every one who laps with his tongue from the water as laps the dog, you shall set him by himself; and every one who kneels on his knees to drink.
pieces: So Gideon took the troops down to the water, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Put everyone who laps up the water with his tongue, the way a dog laps, in one group. Put everyone who kneels down to drink in another."

L.5: So he brought the people down to the water, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Gideon, "Every one who laps from the water with his tongue, as the dog laps, you shall set him by himself; and every one who kneels down on his knees to drink."

R.5: So Gideon took the men down to the water. There {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told him, "Separate the men into two groups. Put those who lap up the water with their tongues, the way a dog does, in one group. Put those who get down on their knees to drink in the other."

decisions.choice: laps with his tongue as a dog laps: the way the man takes the water into his mouth
decisions.reason: A dog drinks by lapping with its tongue. The LORD names one group by this way of drinking; verse 6 adds that those who lapped did it with their hand to their mouth, that is, they scooped the water up and lapped it from the hand. See the note on verse 6.

decisions.choice: you shall set him by himself; and every one who kneels: the second group is named but its verb is left unsaid
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says what to do with the lappers and then simply names the kneelers, without repeating the verb. The sense is that they are put in a group of their own; verse 6 counts the two groups.

decisions.choice: in one group ... in another (Balanced); Separate the men into two groups (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the words the Hebrew leaves out for the second group, so that the sentence is complete. Literal keeps the unfinished form.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י מִסְפַּ֞ר הַֽמֲלַקְקִ֤ים בְּיָדָם֙ אֶל־פִּיהֶ֔ם שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וְכֹל֙ יֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם כָּרְע֥וּ עַל־בִּרְכֵיהֶ֖ם לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת מָֽיִם׃ס
records.gloss: And was the number of the ones lapping with their hand to their mouth three hundred man; and all [the] rest of the people knelt on their knees to drink water.
pieces: The number of those who lapped, bringing the water to their mouths with their hands, was 300 men. All the rest of the troops knelt down to drink.

L.6: And the number of those who lapped with their hand to their mouth was 300 men; and all the rest of the people knelt down on their knees to drink water.

R.6: Only 300 men scooped up water in their hands and lapped it from their hands. All the others got down on their knees to drink.

decisions.choice: those who lapped with their hand to their mouth: the 300 scooped water in a hand and lapped it from the hand
alternatives: the lappers put their mouths to the water like dogs, and the kneelers brought water to their mouths by hand
decisions.reason: As the Hebrew text stands, "with their hand to their mouth" describes the lappers of verse 5. They did not put their faces down to the water; they raised water in a hand and lapped it with the tongue, as a dog laps. The kneelers bent down on their knees, which most naturally means they drank straight from the water. Some old Greek copies place "with their hand to their mouth" differently, which would turn the picture around; the Hebrew order is followed here, and reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: 300 against the rest: the test makes the army small; it does not grade the men
decisions.reason: The text never says that one way of drinking showed better soldiers. The point of the test is the one the LORD gave in verse 2: an army so small that the victory can only be his. Only a few drank in the unusual way, and those few are the ones he keeps (verse 7).

decisions.choice: bringing the water to their mouths with their hands (Balanced); scooped up water in their hands and lapped it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "with their hand to their mouth" means, following the reading in the note above. Readable adds "only" to bring out how few they were.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־גִּדְע֗וֹן בִּשְׁלֹשׁ֩ מֵא֨וֹת הָאִ֤ישׁ הַֽמֲלַקְקִים֙ אוֹשִׁ֣יעַ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֥י אֶת־מִדְיָ֖ן בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְכָל־הָעָ֔ם יֵלְכ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Gideon, by [the] three hundred the men the lapping I will save you, and I will give Midian into your hand; and all the people, let them go each to his place.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Gideon, "With the 300 men who lapped I will save you all, and I will hand Midian over to you. Let all the others go home."

L.7: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Gideon, "By the 300 men who lapped I will save you, and I will give Midian into your hand; and all the people, let them go, each to his place."

R.7: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Gideon, "I will use the 300 men who lapped to save Israel. I will give you victory over the Midianites. Send all the other men home."

decisions.choice: I will save you (plural) ... into your (singular) hand: the people are saved, Gideon leads
decisions.reason: The first "you" is plural: the LORD will rescue Israel. The second is singular: Midian is given into Gideon's hand. The rescue is for the whole people, through Gideon and the 300.

decisions.choice: each to his place: each to his own home
decisions.reason: "His place" is where a man lives. The others are released from the army (compare verse 8, "each to his tents").

decisions.choice: you all (Balanced); Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: English "you" does not show the plural. Balanced writes "you all" and Readable names Israel, so the reader sees that the people as a whole are meant.

records.source: וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶת־צֵדָה֩ הָעָ֨ם בְּיָדָ֜ם וְאֵ֣ת שׁוֹפְרֹֽתֵיהֶ֗ם וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־אִ֤ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ שִׁלַּח֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְאֹֽהָלָ֔יו וּבִשְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת הָאִ֖ישׁ הֶֽחֱזִ֑יק וּמַחֲנֵ֣ה מִדְיָ֔ן הָ֥יָה ל֖וֹ מִתַּ֥חַת בָּעֵֽמֶק׃פ
records.gloss: And they took provision[s], the people, in their hand, and their trumpets; and all [the] men of Israel he sent each to his tents, and on the three hundred men he kept hold; and [the] camp of Midian was to him below in the valley.
pieces: The men who stayed took provisions in their hands, along with their rams' horns. Gideon sent all the other men of Israel back to their tents, but he kept the 300 men. The camp of Midian lay below him in the valley.

L.8: And the people took provisions in their hand, and their trumpets; and all the men of Israel he sent away, each to his tents, but the 300 men he kept; and the camp of Midian was below him in the valley.

R.8: The 300 men took food and trumpets with them. Gideon sent all the other Israelites home, but he kept the 300. The Midianite camp was below him in the valley.

decisions.choice: the people took provisions ... and their trumpets: the 300 who stayed equipped themselves
alternatives: they took the provisions of the people and their trumpets
decisions.reason: The word for "provisions" stands on its own, not joined to "the people", so "the people" is most likely the subject: the men took provisions and trumpets in hand. Since the 300 had a trumpet each in verse 16, the trumpets, and perhaps the jars, may have been gathered from the men who were leaving. With a small change of vowels the clause could read "they took the provisions of the people", that is, the 300 took the supplies of the departing men.

decisions.choice: sent each to his tents: sent them home
decisions.reason: "To your tents" was a way of saying "go home", kept from the time Israel lived in tents (1 Samuel 13:2; 1 Kings 12:16).

decisions.choice: trumpets: rams' horns
decisions.reason: The word is the shofar, a ram's horn blown to give signals, call men to battle, or raise an alarm (3:27; 6:34; Joshua 6:4-5). It is not a metal trumpet.

decisions.choice: The men who stayed (Balanced); The 300 men (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain who "the people" are here, following the reading in m1. Through the chapter the shofar is "trumpet" at Literal and Readable and "ram's horn" or "horn" at Balanced, as in Joshua 6.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה ק֖וּם רֵ֣ד בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה כִּ֥י נְתַתִּ֖יו בְּיָדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And it was in the night, that, and said to him Yahweh, arise, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.
pieces: That same night {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Gideon, "Get up and go down to attack the camp, because I have handed it over to you.

L.9: And it happened in that night, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Arise, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.

R.9: That night {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Gideon, "Get up! Go down and attack the camp. I have already given you victory over it.

decisions.choice: I have given it: a future victory spoken of as already done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form used for completed action. When God promises something, this form presents it as settled, as good as done (verses 14-15; 3:28; 4:14).

decisions.choice: go down against the camp: attack it
decisions.reason: "Go down into" or "against" a camp is a way of saying to attack it; the Israelites were on the slope above the Midianites in the valley (verse 8). In verse 10 the same verb with "to" means only to go down to the camp, to listen.

decisions.choice: already
decisions.reason: Readable adds "already" to bring out the certainty of the past form (m1).

records.heading: A dream in the camp of Midian

records.source: וְאִם־יָרֵ֥א אַתָּ֖ה לָרֶ֑דֶת רֵ֥ד אַתָּ֛ה וּפֻרָ֥ה נַעַרְךָ֖ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And if afraid [are] you to go down, go down you and Purah your servant to the camp,
pieces: But if you are afraid to attack, go down to the camp with Purah your servant,

L.10: But if you [are] afraid to go down, go down, you and Purah your servant, to the camp,

R.10: But if you are afraid to attack, take your servant Purah and go down to the camp first.

decisions.choice: your servant: a young man who attended Gideon
decisions.reason: The word means a young man, and often a young man who serves another, such as an armor-bearer (9:54; 1 Samuel 14:1). It is not the word for a slave.

decisions.choice: if you are afraid: the LORD meets Gideon's fear
decisions.reason: Gideon had asked for signs before (6:17, 36-40). Here the LORD offers him a further assurance without being asked, while still commanding the attack.

decisions.choice: to attack
decisions.reason: "Go down" in the first clause means to go down against the camp, as in verse 9; Balanced and Readable say "attack" so that it is not confused with going down to the camp to listen. Readable adds "first" to show the order of events.

records.source: וְשָֽׁמַעְתָּ֙ מַה־יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ וְאַחַר֙ תֶּחֱזַ֣קְנָה יָדֶ֔יךָ וְיָרַדְתָּ֖ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיֵּ֤רֶד הוּא֙ וּפֻרָ֣ה נַעֲר֔וֹ אֶל־קְצֵ֥ה הַחֲמֻשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: and you will hear what they say, and afterward will be strong your hands, and you will go down against the camp. And went down he and Purah his servant to [the] edge of the ones arrayed for battle who [were] in the camp.
pieces: and listen to what they are saying. After that you will have the courage to attack the camp." So he went down with Purah his servant to the outer edge of the armed men in the camp.

L.11: and you will hear what they say, and afterward your hands will be strong, and you will go down against the camp." And he went down, he and Purah his servant, to the edge of the battle-ready [men] who [were] in the camp.

R.11: Listen to what they are saying. Then you will feel brave enough to attack." So Gideon and his servant Purah went down to the edge of the camp, where the soldiers were.

decisions.choice: your hands will be strong: you will have courage
decisions.reason: Strong hands stand for courage and readiness to act; weak or dropping hands for fear (2 Samuel 2:7; Isaiah 35:3; Zephaniah 3:16).

decisions.choice: the battle-ready men: soldiers armed and in order for battle
decisions.reason: The same word describes Israel leaving Egypt in battle order and the armed men who crossed the Jordan ahead of their brothers (Exodus 13:18; Joshua 1:14; 4:12). Its exact sense is debated; it may be linked with the number five, perhaps for an army drawn up in five parts.

decisions.choice: the edge: the outer part of the camp
decisions.reason: Gideon goes only to the outskirts, where men on guard would be, not into the middle of the camp (compare verses 17, 19).

records.source: וּמִדְיָ֨ן וַעֲמָלֵ֤ק וְכָל־בְּנֵי־קֶ֨דֶם֙ נֹפְלִ֣ים בָּעֵ֔מֶק כָּאַרְבֶּ֖ה לָרֹ֑ב וְלִגְמַלֵּיהֶם֙ אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֔ר כַּח֛וֹל שֶׁעַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיָּ֖ם לָרֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And Midian and Amalek and all [the] sons of [the] east [were] lying in the valley like the locust for multitude; and to their camels there [was] no number, like the sand which [is] on [the] lip of the sea for multitude.
pieces: The Midianites, the Amalekites and all the peoples of the east were spread across the valley as thick as locusts. Their camels were past counting, as many as the grains of sand by the sea.

L.12: And Midian and Amalek and all the sons of the east [were] lying in the valley like locusts for multitude; and their camels [were] without number, like the sand that [is] on the shore of the sea for multitude.

R.12: The Midianites, the Amalekites and the other tribes from the east covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. They had more camels than anyone could count, as many as the grains of sand on the beach.

decisions.choice: Midian, Amalek and the sons of the east: desert peoples who raided Israel
decisions.reason: These are the same allies who came up with their flocks and tents each year and ruined Israel's crops (6:3-5, 33). "The sons of the east" are the tribes of the desert east of the Jordan (Genesis 29:1; Job 1:3).

decisions.choice: like locusts ... like the sand on the seashore: too many to count
decisions.reason: Both pictures stand for a vast number (Genesis 22:17; Joshua 11:4). Locusts also fit the way these peoples stripped the land bare (6:5).

decisions.choice: lying: camped and spread out
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "fall". Here it describes an army lying spread out over the ground in its camp, as in 1 Samuel 30:1.

decisions.choice: the peoples of the east (Balanced); the other tribes from the east (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Sons of" here means members of a people, not children; Balanced and Readable say "peoples" and "tribes".

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣א גִדְע֔וֹן וְהִ֨נֵּה־אִ֔ישׁ מְסַפֵּ֥ר לְרֵעֵ֖הוּ חֲל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הִנֵּ֧ה חֲל֣וֹם חָלַ֗מְתִּי וְהִנֵּ֨ה צְלִ֜יל לֶ֤חֶם שְׂעֹרִים֙ מִתְהַפֵּךְ֙ בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה מִדְיָ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֣א עַד־הָ֠אֹהֶל וַיַּכֵּ֧הוּ וַיִּפֹּ֛ל וַיַּהַפְכֵ֥הוּ לְמַ֖עְלָה וְנָפַ֥ל הָאֹֽהֶל׃
records.gloss: And came Gideon, and look, a man [was] recounting to his companion a dream, and he said, look, a dream I dreamed, and look, a round loaf of bread of barley tumbling into [the] camp of Midian, and it came to the tent and struck it, and it fell, and turned it upward, and fell the tent.
pieces: Just as Gideon arrived, one man was describing a dream to his friend. "Listen," he said, "I had a dream. A round loaf of barley bread came rolling into the camp of Midian. It came to the tent and hit it so hard that it fell. It turned the tent upside down, and the tent collapsed."

L.13: And Gideon came, and look, a man [was] telling a dream to his companion, and he said, "Look, I dreamed a dream, and look, a round loaf of barley bread [was] tumbling into the camp of Midian; and it came to the tent and struck it, and it fell, and it turned it upside down, and the tent lay flat."

R.13: When Gideon got there, he heard a man telling his friend about a dream. The man said, "In my dream I saw a round loaf of barley bread roll into the Midianite camp. It hit the tent so hard that the tent turned over and fell flat."

decisions.choice: a round loaf: the read form of a rare word
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text and the form handed down for reading differ slightly in this word; the pinned data follows the read form. The word comes only here, and its sense is taken from a root meaning "to roll" or "to be round": a round, flat loaf or cake. Reviewers should check this against the manuscript notes.

decisions.choice: barley bread: plain food of farmers
decisions.reason: Barley was cheaper than wheat and was the bread of ordinary and poorer people (2 Kings 4:42; John 6:9). A loaf of farmers' bread knocking over a tent of the desert raiders is a picture of Israel, the people of the field, overturning Midian, the people of tents. Verse 14 gives the friend's reading of it.

decisions.choice: the tent: probably a particular tent, perhaps the leader's
decisions.reason: The word has the article, "the tent", as if one tent stood out in the camp, perhaps the commander's. It may simply mean the tent seen in the dream. "Turned it upward" means turned it upside down, and the last clause sums up: the tent lay flat.

decisions.choice: Listen (Balanced); left out (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "look" three times, drawing attention to what is seen and told. Literal keeps it each time; Balanced uses "Listen" once at the start of the dream, and Readable lets "he heard" and "I saw" carry the sense.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַן רֵעֵ֤הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵ֣ין זֹ֔את בִּלְתִּ֗י אִם־חֶ֛רֶב גִּדְע֥וֹן בֶּן־יוֹאָ֖שׁ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל נָתַ֤ן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ אֶת־מִדְיָ֖ן וְאֶת־כָּל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And answered his companion and said, not [is] this except [the] sword of Gideon son of Joash, a man of Israel; has given God into his hand Midian and all the camp.
pieces: His friend replied, "This can be nothing but the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite! God has handed Midian and the whole army over to him."

L.14: And his companion answered and said, "This [is] nothing except the sword of Gideon son of Joash, a man of Israel. God has given Midian and all the camp into his hand."

R.14: His friend answered, "This must mean the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite. God has given him victory over Midian and our whole army."

decisions.choice: God: a Midianite speaks of Israel's God
decisions.reason: The man uses the general word for God, not the LORD's personal name. The enemy himself admits that Israel's God has decided the battle (compare Rahab in Joshua 2:9-11). When Gideon answers in verse 15, he names the LORD.

decisions.choice: has given: spoken as already done
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, the past form treats the coming defeat as certain. The LORD's promise to Gideon is echoed by an enemy's mouth.

decisions.choice: the sword of Gideon: picked up in the battle cry
decisions.reason: The dream is read as Gideon's sword, and in verse 20 Gideon's men will cry "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!".

decisions.choice: all the camp: the whole army in the camp
decisions.reason: The word for "camp" also means those who are camped there, the army (verses 21-22).

decisions.choice: our whole army
decisions.reason: The speaker is one of the Midianite soldiers; Readable adds "our" to make that clear.

records.source: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ גִּדְע֜וֹן אֶת־מִסְפַּ֧ר הַחֲל֛וֹם וְאֶת־שִׁבְר֖וֹ וַיִּשְׁתָּ֑חוּ וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ אֶל־מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ק֔וּמוּ כִּֽי־נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה בְּיֶדְכֶ֖ם אֶת־מַחֲנֵ֥ה מִדְיָֽן׃
records.gloss: And it was, when heard Gideon the recounting of the dream and its breaking, and he bowed down; and he returned to [the] camp of Israel and said, arise, for has given Yahweh into your hand [the] camp of Midian.
pieces: When Gideon heard the dream and what it meant, he bowed down in worship. Then he went back to the camp of Israel and called out, "Get up! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has handed the camp of Midian over to you."

L.15: And it happened, when Gideon heard the telling of the dream and its interpretation, that he bowed down; and he returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Arise, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given the camp of Midian into your hand."

R.15: When Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to worship. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, "Get up! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given you victory over the Midianite army!"

decisions.choice: its interpretation: literally "its breaking", a word that points to the breaking of the jars
decisions.reason: The usual word for "breaking" is used here, uniquely, for the meaning of a dream: what it breaks open, its solution. The same idea of breaking returns when the men smash their jars (verses 19-20).

decisions.choice: he bowed down: in worship
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow low before someone; with no one else named, it is worship of the LORD, who had sent him to hear the dream (as in Genesis 24:26; Exodus 4:31).

decisions.choice: the LORD has given: the same certainty as in verses 9 and 14
decisions.reason: Gideon now says to his men what the LORD said to him (verse 9) and what the Midianite said (verse 14), using the LORD's name.

decisions.choice: the Midianite army
decisions.reason: "The camp of Midian" here is the army camped there (verse 14); Readable says "army".

records.source: וַיַּ֛חַץ אֶת־שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת הָאִ֖ישׁ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁ֑ים וַיִּתֵּ֨ן שׁוֹפָר֤וֹת בְּיַד־כֻּלָּם֙ וְכַדִּ֣ים רֵקִ֔ים וְלַפִּדִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ הַכַּדִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And he divided the three hundred men [into] three companies, and he put trumpets in [the] hand of all of them, and jars empty, and torches inside the jars.
pieces: He divided the 300 men into three companies and gave each of them a ram's horn and an empty jar, with a torch inside the jar.

L.16: And he divided the 300 men [into] three companies, and he put trumpets in the hand of all of them, and empty jars, with torches inside the jars.

R.16: Gideon divided the 300 men into three groups. He gave each man a trumpet and an empty clay jar with a burning torch inside it.

decisions.choice: companies: literally "heads"
decisions.reason: "Heads" is used for divisions of an army, each with its own leader (9:34, 43; 1 Samuel 11:11; 13:17).

decisions.choice: torches inside empty jars: lights hidden until the signal
decisions.reason: The jars were pottery jars, the kind used for carrying water (Genesis 24:14). A lit torch inside a jar could be carried at night without being seen, and shown all at once when the jar was broken (verse 20).

decisions.choice: trumpets: rams' horns, one for each man
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, the shofar is a ram's horn. Normally only a few men in an army would blow horns, so 300 horns at once would sound like a very large force.

decisions.choice: clay; burning
decisions.reason: Readable adds that the jars were clay, which is why they could be smashed, and that the torches were burning, which the Hebrew takes for granted (verse 20).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם מִמֶּ֥נִּי תִרְא֖וּ וְכֵ֣ן תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ וְהִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֥י בָא֙ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה כַאֲשֶׁר־אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה כֵּ֥ן תַּעֲשֽׂוּן׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, from me you will see, and thus you will do; and look, I [am] coming into [the] edge of the camp, and it will be, as I do, so you will do.
pieces: "Watch me," he told them, "and do what I do. When I reach the edge of the camp, do exactly as I do.

L.17: And he said to them, "Look at me, and do likewise. And look, [when] I come to the edge of the camp, then it shall be: as I do, so you shall do.

R.17: He told them, "Watch me and do what I do. When I get to the edge of the camp, do just what I do.

decisions.choice: from me you will see: watch me and take your lead from me
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "from me you will see", meaning "learn from what I do". Gideon's men are to copy his signals exactly.

decisions.choice: look, I am coming: when I come
decisions.reason: "Look" with a participle points to what is about to happen; here it sets the time for the command that follows.

records.source: וְתָקַעְתִּי֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר אָנֹכִ֖י וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתִּ֑י וּתְקַעְתֶּ֨ם בַּשּׁוֹפָר֜וֹת גַּם־אַתֶּ֗ם סְבִיבוֹת֙ כָּל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם לַיהוָ֥ה וּלְגִדְעֽוֹן׃פ
records.gloss: And I will blow on the trumpet, I and all who [are] with me, and you will blow on the trumpets, also you, all around all the camp, and you will say, for Yahweh and for Gideon.
pieces: When I blow my horn, along with everyone who is with me, you are to blow your horns too, on every side of the camp, and shout, 'For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for Gideon!'"

L.18: And [when] I blow on the trumpet, I and all who [are] with me, then you also shall blow on the trumpets all around the whole camp, and you shall say, 'For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for Gideon!'"

R.18: When my group and I blow our trumpets, all of you on every side of the camp must blow your trumpets too. Then shout, 'For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for Gideon!'"

decisions.choice: For the LORD and for Gideon: a short battle cry
decisions.reason: The cry names the one the battle is fought for and the leader he has chosen. When the men actually shout it in verse 20, they say it in a fuller form: "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"

decisions.choice: all around the whole camp: the three companies surround the camp
decisions.reason: With 100 men in each company (verses 16, 19), Gideon's force is spread around the camp so that the noise and lights come from every side.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣א גִ֠דְעוֹן וּמֵאָה־אִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֜וֹ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֗ה רֹ֚אשׁ הָאַשְׁמֹ֣רֶת הַתִּֽיכוֹנָ֔ה אַ֛ךְ הָקֵ֥ם הֵקִ֖ימוּ אֶת־הַשֹּֽׁמְרִ֑ים וַֽיִּתְקְעוּ֙ בַּשּׁ֣וֹפָר֔וֹת וְנָפ֥וֹץ הַכַּדִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּיָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And came Gideon and [the] hundred men who [were] with him to [the] edge of the camp [at the] beginning of the watch, the middle; only establishing they had established the watchmen; and they blew on the trumpets, and smashing the jars which [were] in their hand.
pieces: Gideon and the 100 men with him reached the edge of the camp at the start of the middle watch of the night, just after the new guards had been posted. They blew their horns and smashed the jars they were holding.

L.19: And Gideon and the 100 men who [were] with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, when they had just posted the watchmen; and they blew on the trumpets and smashed the jars that [were] in their hand.

R.19: Gideon and his 100 men reached the edge of the camp in the middle of the night, at the start of the second watch, just after the Midianites had changed guards. The men blew their trumpets and smashed the jars they were carrying.

decisions.choice: the beginning of the middle watch: some hours after dark
decisions.reason: Israel divided the night into three watches (Lamentations 2:19 speaks of the beginning of the watches; Exodus 14:24 and 1 Samuel 11:11 of the morning watch). The middle watch ran through the middle of the night, from about late evening to the small hours. The camp would be asleep, and the guards new at their posts.

decisions.choice: they had just posted the watchmen: the Midianites had only now changed guard
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis, with "only" before it: the new guards had only just been set. "They" are the Midianites. Fresh guards who did not yet know their surroundings, and the men just going off duty, would make the alarm all the greater.

decisions.choice: smashing: and they smashed
decisions.reason: The verb is in a form that simply names the action without person or tense; following "they blew", it continues the narrative: they blew and smashed.

decisions.choice: in the middle of the night, at the start of the second watch
decisions.reason: Readable explains the time and says that the middle of three watches is the second one.

records.heading: Trumpets, jars and torches

records.source: וַֽ֠יִּתְקְעוּ שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת הָרָאשִׁ֥ים בַּשּֽׁוֹפָרוֹת֮ וַיִּשְׁבְּר֣וּ הַכַּדִּים֒ וַיַּחֲזִ֤יקוּ בְיַד־שְׂמאוֹלָם֙בַּלַּפִּדִ֔ים וּבְיַ֨ד־יְמִינָ֔ם הַשּׁוֹפָר֖וֹת לִתְק֑וֹעַ וַֽיִּקְרְא֔וּ חֶ֥רֶב לַֽיהוָ֖ה וּלְגִדְעֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And blew [the] three [of] the companies on the trumpets, and they broke the jars, and they held in [the] hand of their left on the torches, and in [the] hand of their right the trumpets to blow; and they called out, a sword for Yahweh and for Gideon.
pieces: All three companies blew their horns and broke their jars. With the torches in their left hands and the horns for blowing in their right, they shouted, "A sword for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for Gideon!"

L.20: And the three companies blew on the trumpets and broke the jars, and they held the torches in their left hand and the trumpets in their right hand to blow; and they cried out, "A sword for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for Gideon!"

R.20: Then all three groups blew their trumpets and broke their jars. Each man had his torch in his left hand and his trumpet in his right, ready to blow. They all shouted, "A sword for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and for Gideon!"

decisions.choice: A sword for the LORD and for Gideon: the sword fights on the LORD's behalf and on Gideon's
alternatives: The sword of the LORD and of Gideon!
decisions.reason: The cry has no verb: "a sword for the LORD and for Gideon". The word "for" marks those on whose behalf the sword is drawn, and to whom the victory will belong. It is also often understood as "the sword of the LORD and of Gideon", which comes to much the same; the Hebrew does not say "the" or "of".

decisions.choice: no sword in hand: the LORD's sword does the fighting
decisions.reason: Each man has a torch in one hand and a horn in the other, so no one is holding a sword. The cry echoes the Midianite's reading of the dream ("the sword of Gideon", verse 14), and in verse 22 it is the LORD who turns the enemy's swords against each other.

decisions.choice: they broke the jars: the torches blaze out at once
decisions.reason: Breaking the jars uncovered the torches in a single moment, so that 300 lights and 300 horns seemed to come from a great army on every side.

records.source: וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ תַּחְתָּ֔יו סָבִ֖יב לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיָּ֧רָץ כָּל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֛ה וַיָּרִ֖יעוּ וַיָּנֽוּסוּ׃
records.gloss: And they stood each in his place all around the camp; and ran all the camp, and they cried out, and they fled.
pieces: Each man stood in his place around the camp, while the whole Midianite army ran about, shouting, and fled.

L.21: And they stood, each in his place, all around the camp; and all the camp ran, and they cried out and fled.

R.21: Every Israelite stayed where he stood around the camp. The whole Midianite army began running and yelling and trying to get away.

decisions.choice: they fled: the read form
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text could be read "they made [others] flee" or "they put to flight"; the form handed down for reading is "they fled", and the pinned data follows it. The sense is the same either way: the camp broke up in flight. Reviewers should check this against the manuscript notes.

decisions.choice: each stood in his place: Israel does not attack
decisions.reason: Gideon's men hold their positions; the enemy defeats itself. The victory is the LORD's, as verse 2 said it must be (compare Exodus 14:13-14).

decisions.choice: all the camp ran and cried out: the army in panic
decisions.reason: "The camp" is the army camped in it, as in verse 14. The verb for crying out is used for a shout of alarm or a war cry; here it is the cry of men in terror.

decisions.choice: Midianite (Balanced, Readable); Israelite (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew changes from Gideon's men to the enemy without naming either. Balanced and Readable add the names so that the reader can follow who is doing what.

records.source: וַֽיִּתְקְעוּ֮ שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֣וֹת הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת֒ וַיָּ֣שֶׂם יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֣ת חֶ֥רֶב אִ֛ישׁ בְּרֵעֵ֖הוּ וּבְכָל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיָּ֨נָס הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֜ה עַד־בֵּ֤ית הַשִּׁטָּה֙ צְֽרֵרָ֔תָה עַ֛ד שְׂפַת־אָבֵ֥ל מְחוֹלָ֖ה עַל־טַבָּֽת׃
records.gloss: And they blew, [the] three hundred, the trumpets, and set Yahweh [the] sword of each against his companion and in all the camp; and fled the camp as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as [the] lip of Abel-meholah by Tabbath.
pieces: When the 300 blew their horns, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned every man's sword against his comrade throughout the whole army. The army fled toward Zererah as far as Beth-shittah, and as far as the edge of Abel-meholah near Tabbath.

L.22: And the 300 blew the trumpets, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} set the sword of each man against his companion, and throughout the whole camp; and the camp fled as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as the edge of Abel-meholah, by Tabbath.

R.22: As the 300 men blew their trumpets, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the Midianite soldiers attack one another with their swords all through the camp. The army ran away toward Zererah, as far as Beth-shittah, and on as far as the edge of Abel-meholah near Tabbath.

decisions.choice: the LORD set each man's sword against his companion: the enemy destroys itself
decisions.reason: In the dark and the panic the Midianites took each other for the enemy. The text says that the LORD brought this about. The same thing happens in other battles the LORD wins for Israel (1 Samuel 14:20; 2 Chronicles 20:23).

decisions.choice: Beth-shittah, Zererah, Abel-meholah, Tabbath: places on the way down to the Jordan
decisions.reason: The army fled east and south-east from the Valley of Jezreel toward the Jordan valley. Abel-meholah, later the home of Elisha (1 Kings 19:16), lay near the Jordan; the other places cannot be located with certainty.

decisions.choice: the edge: literally "the lip"
decisions.reason: The word for "lip" is used for an edge or border, as of the seashore in verse 12. Here it may mean the border of Abel-meholah's land, or the edge of the river near it.

decisions.choice: made the Midianite soldiers attack one another
decisions.reason: Readable names the Midianites and says plainly what "set each man's sword against his companion" means.

records.source: וַיִּצָּעֵ֧ק אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מִנַּפְתָּלִ֥י וּמִן־אָשֵׁ֖ר וּמִן־כָּל־מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י מִדְיָֽן׃
records.gloss: And was called out [the] man of Israel from Naphtali and from Asher and from all Manasseh, and they pursued after Midian.
pieces: Then the men of Israel from Naphtali, Asher and all Manasseh were called to arms, and they chased the Midianites.

L.23: And the men of Israel were called out from Naphtali and from Asher and from all Manasseh, and they pursued after Midian.

R.23: Then men from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher and all of Manasseh were called out to fight, and they chased the Midianites.

decisions.choice: the man of Israel: the men of Israel as one body
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses "man" in the singular for the fighting men of Israel taken together (as in 20:11).

decisions.choice: were called out: summoned to arms
decisions.reason: This form of the verb "cry out" means to be called together for battle (6:34-35; 12:1; 1 Samuel 13:4).

decisions.choice: Naphtali, Asher, Manasseh: tribes Gideon had called before
decisions.reason: These tribes, with Zebulun, had answered Gideon's first call (6:35). The men now called out probably include some of those he had just sent home (verses 7-8), joining in once the enemy was on the run.

decisions.choice: chased the Midianites
decisions.reason: "Midian" is the people; Balanced and Readable say "the Midianites".

records.source: וּמַלְאָכִ֡ים שָׁלַ֣ח גִּדְעוֹן֩ בְּכָל־הַ֨ר אֶפְרַ֜יִם לֵאמֹ֗ר רְד֞וּ לִקְרַ֤את מִדְיָן֙ וְלִכְד֤וּ לָהֶם֙ אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם עַ֛ד בֵּ֥ית בָּרָ֖ה וְאֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וַיִּצָּעֵ֞ק כָּל־אִ֤ישׁ אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ וַיִּלְכְּד֣וּ אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם עַ֛ד בֵּ֥ית בָּרָ֖ה וְאֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And messengers sent Gideon in all [the] hill country of Ephraim, saying, come down to meet Midian, and capture before them the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan. And was called out every man of Ephraim, and they captured the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan.
pieces: Gideon sent messengers all through the hill country of Ephraim with this message: "Come down against the Midianites and take the waters ahead of them as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan as well." So all the men of Ephraim were called out, and they took the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan.

L.24: And Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down to meet Midian, and capture the waters ahead of them as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan." And every man of Ephraim was called out, and they captured the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan.

R.24: Gideon sent messengers all through the hill country of Ephraim. They said, "Come down and fight the Midianites. Get to the river crossings before they do, as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan River." So all the men of Ephraim were called out. They took control of the river crossings as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan.

decisions.choice: the waters: the streams and fords on the way to the Jordan
decisions.reason: To escape home, the Midianites had to cross the Jordan and the streams running down to it. Holding the fords cut off their escape, as Ehud's men did against Moab (3:28) and the Gileadites later against Ephraim (12:5-6).

decisions.choice: come down to meet Midian: come down against them
decisions.reason: "To meet" an enemy is to go out against him in battle (as in 20:25; 1 Samuel 4:1).

decisions.choice: and the Jordan: the Jordan as well
decisions.reason: "And the Jordan" is added after "as far as Beth-barah". It may mean the Jordan's own crossings besides the streams, or it may explain "the waters" as the Jordan itself. Either way the aim is to hold the river line.

decisions.choice: Ephraim: the tribe in the central hills
decisions.reason: Ephraim had not been called before (6:35). Its men come in now at the end, which leads to their complaint in 8:1.

decisions.choice: the river crossings
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the waters" were for in this battle: the places where the fleeing army could cross.

records.source: וַֽיִּלְכְּד֡וּ שְׁנֵֽי־שָׂרֵ֨י מִדְיָ֜ן אֶת־עֹרֵ֣ב וְאֶת־זְאֵ֗ב וַיַּהַרְג֨וּ אֶת־עוֹרֵ֤ב בְּצוּר־עוֹרֵב֙ וְאֶת־זְאֵב֙ הָרְג֣וּ בְיֶֽקֶב־זְאֵ֔ב וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֖וּ אֶל־מִדְיָ֑ן וְרֹאשׁ־עֹרֵ֣ב וּזְאֵ֔ב הֵבִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶל־גִּדְע֔וֹן מֵעֵ֖בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And they captured [the] two commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and they killed Oreb at [the] rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they killed at [the] winepress of Zeeb; and they pursued to Midian; and [the] head of Oreb and Zeeb they brought to Gideon from across the Jordan.
pieces: They also captured the two commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. Oreb they killed at the Rock of Oreb, and Zeeb at the Winepress of Zeeb. They kept up the pursuit of the Midianites, and they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon from across the Jordan.

L.25: And they captured the two commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they killed at the winepress of Zeeb; and they pursued Midian; and the head of Oreb and Zeeb they brought to Gideon from across the Jordan.

R.25: The men of Ephraim also captured two Midianite commanders named Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the place called the Rock of Oreb and Zeeb at the place called the Winepress of Zeeb. They kept chasing the Midianites, and they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon from the other side of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: Oreb and Zeeb: "raven" and "wolf"
decisions.reason: The two names mean "raven" and "wolf". The places where they died were known by their names, and later Scripture remembers their fall as a great act of the LORD (Isaiah 10:26; Psalm 83:12).

decisions.choice: the two commanders of Midian: army leaders, not the kings
decisions.reason: Oreb and Zeeb were leaders of the Midianite forces. The two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, escape across the Jordan and are pursued in chapter 8 (8:5, 10-12).

decisions.choice: from across the Jordan: the place of Gideon or of the heads is not certain
alternatives: to Gideon, who was across the Jordan
decisions.reason: The phrase may say where the heads came from, or where Gideon was when they reached him. The story of the crossing comes only in 8:4, so the narrator may be summing up the end of the pursuit here before going back to tell it. The wording is kept open at every level.

decisions.choice: the heads: proof that the enemy leaders were dead
decisions.reason: A victor brought back an enemy's head as proof of his death (1 Samuel 17:54; 31:9). The Hebrew has "head" in the singular, as a word for each of them.

decisions.choice: commanders
decisions.reason: The word often means "princes" or "officials"; in this military setting it is "commanders" at every level.

decisions.choice: The men of Ephraim
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they"; verse 24 shows that the men of Ephraim are meant, and Readable names them.
